RECOMMENDED INTERVENTION: TEMPORARY CALCAREOUS SCALE FORMATION AT COATING DEFECTS

The proposed intervention temporarily raises the rectifier output to establish a pipe-to-soil potential of -0.95 V vs. Cu/CuSO4 (CSE) at remote test stations for a defined duration, then steps back to -0.85 V CSE. This temporary overprotection triggers the precipitation of calcareous deposits (CaCO3 and Ca(OH)2) on exposed bare steel at coating holidays. The resulting mineral scale layer reduces the effective bare-metal surface area, thereby lowering the anodic current demand per kilometer. This reduces the total load on the fixed rectifier power budget, allowing the far-end potentials to shift from the failing -0.72 V toward the -0.85 V criterion without exceeding the available amperage.

PARAMETER: Temporary overprotection potential — -0.95 V vs CSE — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Target maintenance potential — -0.85 V vs CSE — ASSUMPTION 
PARAMETER: Baseline failing potential — -0.72 V vs CSE — EVIDENCE-BACKED [USER_VARIABLES]
PARAMETER: Coating defect size range — 0.2 mm to 1.0 mm pinholes — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Soil resistivity — 100 ohm-m — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Rectifier output limit — Fixed maximum amperage A_max — EVIDENCE-BACKED [USER_VARIABLES]

CONSTRAINT COMPLIANCE:
No pipeline excavation is permitted; this method utilizes existing rectifier controls and remote potential monitoring only. The rectifier power budget is fixed; the intervention does not require additional amperage capacity but rather optimizes the distribution of existing current by reducing the load at the far ends via defect passivation. The device remains the 36-inch coal-tar enamel transmission pipeline; no physical alteration to the pipe or coating is made, only the electrochemical environment at existing defects is modified.

FALSIFICATION TEST:
Protocol: Conduct a temporary overprotection campaign on the affected remote section.
Test Temperature: 15 C ambient soil temperature.
Duration: 30 days of continuous operation at -0.95 V CSE.
Sample Size n: 10 remote test stations located at the far end of the protected section.
Pass Criteria: After 30 days, at least 8 out of 10 test stations must read a stable potential of -0.85 V CSE or more negative while the rectifier output current remains below 90% of its fixed maximum rated capacity.
Fail Criteria: If fewer than 8 stations achieve -0.85 V CSE, or if rectifier output exceeds 90% of its fixed budget for more than 24 hours during the campaign, the hypothesis that calcareous scale formation sufficiently reduces holiday current drain is falsified.

EVIDENCE NOTE: The mechanism relies on established electrochemical principles of cathodic protection in aerated soils, where overprotection drives calcareous deposition. The target potential of -0.85 V CSE is the standard protection criterion for buried steel in soil [NACE SP0285-2005-03]. The baseline failing potential of -0.72 V and the fixed rectifier power budget are user-stated variables. The defect size and soil resistivity are engineering assumptions based on typical 1970s-era pipeline degradation profiles.
